title: Exporters divert cement to UK following new EU carbon border rules
summary: Exporters divert cement to UK following new EU carbon border rules
body_markdown:
**Europe:** Non-EU cement accounted for 29% of UK cement imports in the first nine months of 2026, up by 17% year-on-year from the same period in 2025, according to Mineral Products Association (MPA) analysis of figures from UK customs. The share was its highest since records began in 2000.


The MPA attributed the shift to the EU’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), which came into effect in January 2026. The UK will launch its own CBAM on 1 January 2027, but its illustrative tax rates are lower than the EU’s and it will not adopt country-specific default emissions values until 2029.


MPA senior director for cement and lime Martin Casey said “Our manufacturers are operating at an unfair disadvantage and we need to close the competitiveness gap between the emissions costs faced by domestic producers and those faced by overseas competitors.” Casey called for the UK government to link its emissions trading scheme with the EU’s and align its CBAM more closely with the bloc’s regime.
